messages:
Isabella Rossi: quick perf update on the extra stream/event sync around NCCL collectives (from PR-21853).

Ran microbench on A100 80GB (8x, TP=8) w/ mixed prefill+decode + pure decode loops.

TL;DR: looks like a small but non-zero hit. Biggest regressions show up in tight decode-only loops.

Numbers (median of 10 runs, same clocks):
```
config: TP=8, bs=8, seq_in=128, gen=256, fp16, no cuda graphs
baseline (main):     100% (ref)
+sync hardening:      -2.1% tok/s

config: TP=8, bs=1, seq_in=32, gen=512 (decode-heavy)
baseline (main):     100% (ref)
+sync hardening:      -8.7% tok/s

config: TP=8, bs=16, seq_in=2048, gen=64 (prefill-heavy)
baseline (main):     100% (ref)
+sync hardening:      -1.3% tok/s
```
Also saw p50 per-step decode latency go from ~3.9ms -> ~4.3ms in the decode-heavy case.

I didn’t test CUDA graph capture yet (that path has different stream semantics).

Happy to rerun on H100 if someone has a spare window in perf-lab.

Grace Kim: thx. is this with the full `cudaEventRecord + cudaStreamWaitEvent` around every collective? or just the pre/post fence we added?

Isabella Rossi: full version currently in the PR: pre-collective event on compute stream, wait on nccl stream; then post-collective event on nccl stream, wait back on compute stream.

Yuki Sato: -8.7% on decode-only is… not great. but also that’s the tightest loop / worst case. real workloads have more compute between collectives.

Marcus Reed: do we have end-to-end numbers from perf-canary style workloads? microbench is useful but might overstate impact.

Isabella Rossi: not yet. i can port it to the perf harness but it’ll take me ~half day.

Hiro Tanaka: the 8-9% is within the range I worried about if we force a hard sync per token step.

Question: can we reduce frequency? e.g. only enforce ordering at “step boundaries” (prefill boundary + every N decode iters) vs every collective call.

Noah Patel: we need to be careful there. if the hang is from collective ordering mismatch, skipping fences on some iters might reintroduce it.

But: we might be able to avoid the *bidirectional* wait every time. maybe it’s enough to ensure nccl stream sees all compute deps before launching collective, and then rely on existing dependencies for the return path.

Grace Kim: right now we’re doing both directions because we saw cases where compute kept running ahead and then blocked later in weird places.

Julian Moore: from sched side, the stall signatures we saw looked like ranks diverging on which stream got ahead, and then NCCL waits forever. I’m okay paying a couple % if it prevents Sev1, but 9% on decode loops will show up on cost.

Yuki Sato: can we gate this behind a feature flag and default it ON only for TP replicas? (and maybe only for affected GPU arch / models)

Grace Kim: it’s already only in TP path, but not feature flagged yet. we could add `runtime.tp.nccl_stream_sync_hardening` and keep default off for Hosted until canary.

Hiro Tanaka: +1 on flag. also: can we special-case when CUDA graphs are enabled? graph capture already constrains streams; extra events might not be needed and could be harmful.

Noah Patel: agree. also for CUDA graphs: inserting events can break capture depending on how it’s done. we should make sure PR doesn’t regress graph path.

Isabella Rossi: fwiw, these runs were graph OFF. I can test graph ON too, but we’ll need to use the capture-friendly build.

Marcus Reed: proposal:
- add flag default OFF
- run canary perf suite with flag ON for TP stress scenarios (long context + bursty concurrency)
- if end-to-end regression is <2-3%, we can accept turning it on for Dedicated first

Yuki Sato: +1. the microbench decode-only is worst-case. if canary shows ~2% it’s fine.

Grace Kim: ok i’ll add the flag + wiring in PR-21853 today.

Noah Patel: also: let’s document in the PR that the goal is correctness (avoid silent stall), and perf tradeoff is expected + monitored.

Hiro Tanaka: Isabella, can you run one more microbench where you increase bs a bit for decode? like bs=4 gen=512. want to see if the -9% collapses once there’s more compute.

Isabella Rossi: yep, can do. i’ll reply w/ updated table.

Isabella Rossi: update: A100 TP=8, bs=4, seq_in=32, gen=512:
```
baseline: 100%
+sync:    -3.6% tok/s
```
So the huge hit seems tied to bs=1 decode loop.

Julian Moore: that’s more reassuring. plenty of Dedicated workloads still have bs=1 though (streaming chat).

Yuki Sato: but even streaming chat has more CPU-side overhead and tokenizer + network jitter; not as tight as microbench. still, we should track.

Marcus Reed: action items:
- Isabella: run H100 when available + graph ON/OFF comparison
- Grace: add flag + default OFF; also see if we can avoid post-collective wait back to compute stream without reintroducing risk
- Marcus: add canary perf run w/ flag ON and share deltas

Grace Kim: ack. will post PR update + ping for review. :thumbsup:

Hiro Tanaka: thx all. let’s not ship this unflagged.

Noah Patel: +1. also once flag exists we can do Dedicated-first rollout and tie it to the hang signature dashboards.

Isabella Rossi: cool, will follow up in a thread once i get H100 numbers.
